title: Unit I – Data Structures & Algorithms: Searching, Sorting and Hashing
description: Foundational concepts of algorithmic analysis, asymptotic notations, step-count/frequency count, searching algorithms, sorting methods, hash tables, and collision resolution.

caseStudy.title: Employee Records Database Optimization
caseStudy.scenario: A corporation with thousands of employees needs high-speed lookups by employee salary and batch sorting by department using array-based linear data structures.
caseStudy.learningOutcome: Evaluate trade-offs between linear search vs binary search on sorted employee arrays, and implement in-place quick/merge sort algorithms.

topics.title: Introduction to Data Structures & Types
topics.description: Classification of data structures into primitive, non-primitive, linear, non-linear, static, and dynamic.

topics.title: Complexity Analysis & Asymptotic Notations
topics.description: Time complexity, space complexity, Big-O, Big-Omega, Big-Theta, step-count, and frequency count analysis.

topics.title: Searching Algorithms
topics.description: Sequential (linear) search and binary search with iterative and recursive divide-and-conquer formulations.

topics.title: Sorting Algorithms
topics.description: Insertion sort, bubble sort, selection sort, merge sort, quick sort, and radix sort with pass-by-pass dry runs.

topics.title: Hash Tables & Collision Resolution
topics.description: Hash functions, collision resolution via chaining, open addressing (linear probing, quadratic probing, double hashing), and overflow handling.

topics.title: Unit I Case Study: Employee Records Optimization
topics.description: Practical application of search and sort optimizations on fixed employee records.

title: Unit II – Memory Allocation and Linked List Operations
description: Static vs dynamic memory allocation in C, Singly Linked List, Doubly Linked List, Circular Linked Lists, Polynomial manipulation, and Generalized Linked Lists (GLL).

caseStudy.title: Dynamically Growing Employee Database
caseStudy.scenario: Designing a scalable enterprise human resources directory that avoids array reallocation overheads using singly and doubly linked list pointer chains.
caseStudy.learningOutcome: Master runtime node allocation, zero-memory-waste employee insertion, intermediate deletion, and efficient pointer traversal.

topics.title: Memory Allocation Concepts
topics.description: Static memory allocation (stack/data segment) vs Dynamic memory allocation (heap via malloc, calloc, realloc, free).

topics.title: Singly Linked List as ADT & Operations
topics.description: Node structure, head pointer, traversal, search, insertion (beginning, middle/after pos P, end), and intermediate node deletion.

topics.title: Doubly & Circular Linked Lists
topics.description: Doubly linked list (prev and next pointers), circular singly linked list, doubly circular linked list, and bidirectional traversal.

topics.title: Concatenation, Sorting & Polynomial Operations
topics.description: List concatenation, sorting pointer nodes, polynomial representation and algebraic addition of two polynomials using linked lists.

topics.title: Generalized Linked List (GLL)
topics.description: Definition, representation of non-atomic lists, head and tail, depth calculation, and recursive list structures.

topics.title: Unit II Case Study: Dynamic Enterprise HR Directory
topics.description: Real-world dynamic database implementation using linked lists.

title: Unit III – Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
description: LIFO Stack ADT, sequential and linked stack implementations, expression evaluation, infix-to-postfix conversion, recursion simulation, FIFO Queue ADT, Circular Queue, Deque, and Priority Queue.

caseStudy.title: Backtracking & OS Priority Job Scheduling
caseStudy.scenario: Simulating system execution stacks for backtracking maze solutions and an Operating System real-time job dispatcher with priority queues.
caseStudy.learningOutcome: Understand activation records during recursive depth backtracking and priority queue scheduling algorithms.

topics.title: Stack as ADT & Operations
topics.description: LIFO principle, push, pop, peek, isEmpty, isFull using sequential array and linked representation.

topics.title: Expression Evaluation & Conversion
topics.description: Infix, Prefix, and Postfix notations; Infix-to-Postfix conversion (Shunting-Yard algorithm) and Postfix evaluation with stack traces.

topics.title: Recursion & System Call Stack
topics.description: How compilers execute recursive functions using stack activation frames, local storage, return addresses, and unwinding.

topics.title: Queue ADT & Circular Queue
topics.description: FIFO queue, linear queue limitations (false overflow), circular queue with modulo arithmetic, front/rear pointers, enqueue and dequeue.

topics.title: Double-Ended Queue (Deque) & Priority Queue
topics.description: Input-restricted and output-restricted Deque, Ascending/Descending Priority Queues, array and heap representations.

topics.title: Unit III Case Studies: Backtracking & Job Scheduling
topics.description: Backtracking algorithmic strategy via stack and job queue simulation in an automated service system.

title: Unit IV – Non-Linear Data Structure: Trees
description: Tree terminologies, binary trees, binary tree traversals (Inorder, Preorder, Postorder, Level-order), Binary Search Trees (BST), Threaded Binary Trees, Optimal BST (OBST), Height-balanced AVL Trees, and Heap Trees.

caseStudy.title: Complexity Comparison: BST Search vs Linear Search
caseStudy.scenario: Empirical and theoretical benchmark comparing linear array scans against balanced binary search trees across million-record datasets.
caseStudy.learningOutcome: Analyze average case O(log n) vs worst case skewed O(n) performance and understand height-balanced self-balancing trees.

topics.title: Tree Terminologies & Binary Tree Representations
topics.description: Root, leaf, parent, child, degree, depth, height, level; sequential array representation and doubly linked node representation.

topics.title: Binary Tree Traversals
topics.description: Recursive and iterative Inorder, Preorder, Postorder, and Level-order (BFS queue-based) tree traversal algorithms.

topics.title: Binary Search Tree (BST)
topics.description: BST property, search algorithm, node insertion, and deletion with three cases (leaf, single child, two children with inorder successor/predecessor).

topics.title: Threaded Binary Search Trees (TBST)
topics.description: Single and double threading, replacing dangling NULL pointers with traversal threads, insertion, and stackless inorder traversal.

topics.title: AVL Trees & Optimal Binary Search Tree (OBST)
topics.description: Balance factor calculation, 4 rotation types (LL, RR, LR, RL) with numerical constructions; OBST dynamic programming formulation.

topics.title: Heap Trees & Heap Sort
topics.description: Max-heap, min-heap properties, array mapping, Heapify algorithm, and in-place Heap Sort algorithm.

topics.title: Unit IV Case Study: BST Search vs Linear Search Benchmark
topics.description: Analytical comparison of linear and logarithmic search under skewed and balanced tree configurations.

title: Unit V – Non-Linear Data Structure: Graphs
description: Graph terminologies, graph storage representations (Adjacency Matrix and Adjacency List), Graph Traversals (DFS and BFS), Minimum Spanning Trees (Prim's and Kruskal's), Shortest Path (Dijkstra and Floyd-Warshall), and Topological Ordering.

caseStudy.title: Social Network Interaction & Influence Analysis
caseStudy.scenario: Modeling social media users as graph vertices and friendship/follows as edges to calculate degree centrality, mutual connections, and degrees of separation.
caseStudy.learningOutcome: Apply BFS for shortest social hops and Dijkstra/Kruskal algorithms for minimal network communications infrastructure.

topics.title: Graph Terminologies & Storage Representations
topics.description: Vertices, edges, directed/undirected, weighted, cyclic/acyclic, degree; space and time trade-offs between Adjacency Matrix and Adjacency List.

topics.title: Graph Traversals: DFS and BFS
topics.description: Depth First Search using recursion/stack and Breadth First Search using queue, with visited array tracking and connectivity checking.

topics.title: Minimum Spanning Tree (MST): Prim's & Kruskal's
topics.description: Cut property, Prim's greedy algorithm (vertex growing), and Kruskal's greedy algorithm (edge sorting + Disjoint Set Union).

topics.title: Shortest Paths: Dijkstra & Floyd-Warshall
topics.description: Dijkstra's single-source shortest path algorithm (relaxation steps) and Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path dynamic programming iterations.

topics.title: Topological Ordering & Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAG)
topics.description: Course prerequisite scheduling, indegree calculation, Kahn's algorithm using queue, and cycle detection.

topics.title: Unit V Case Study: Social Network Analysis & Influence
topics.description: Real-world graph modeling of friendships, influence clusters, and 6-degrees-of-separation routing.
